presenters.name: Matt Gracie ⓘ
presenters.bio: Matthew Gracie is a defensive security specialist with fifteen years of Blue Team experience in higher education, manufacturing, financial services, and healthcare. He is currently a Senior Engineer at Security Onion Solutions, as well as an adjunct professor of Cybersecurity in the graduate school at Canisius University. Matt is also the lead organizer of Infosec 716, a monthly meetup for security enthusiasts in Western New York, and the BSides Buffalo technology conference. He enjoys microcontrollers, mountain bikes, open source security tools, and college hockey, and can be found on Bluesky as @InfosecGoon.

schedule.topic: Breakfast Session - Security Onion: What's New? ⓘ
schedule.description: We've made a lot of changes to Security Onion since our last conference - join me for a recap of what's new and some tips and tricks that you can use in your own environment!

presenters.name: Scott Lynch ⓘ
presenters.bio: Scott Lynch is a Senior Engineer at Security Onion Solutions, where he helps commercial and government clients deploy, maintain, and optimize Security Onion for threat detection and security monitoring. He is also a SANS Certified Instructor and course author specializing in SIEM engineering and tactical analytics, teaching detection and response to security professionals worldwide. Scott spent more than two decades in satellite communications and IT security before joining Security Onion Solutions. His career began in the U.S. Navy as an Electronic Warfare specialist aboard a Nimitz class aircraft carrier. He later joined Universal Space Network, founded by Apollo 12 astronaut Charles 'Pete' Conrad, supporting global satellite ground station engineering, operations and mission integration.

schedule.topic: How Can You Hunt If You Don't Know What's on Your Network? ⓘ
schedule.description: Whether you're an attacker or a defender, your first challenge is the same: understand the environment. Before an attacker can compromise a network, they have to figure out where they landed. Reconnaissance against systems, users, services, and trust relationships builds them a map. Defenders need that same map before they can monitor, hunt, or detect anything: what's on the network, how those systems talk to each other, and what 'normal' actually looks like. Too often, security teams investigate alerts referencing systems that appear in no inventory and match no baseline. Analysts burn hours establishing whether a host is even supposed to be there, false positives pile up, and real adversary activity slips past while everyone is busy chasing ghosts. If you don't know what's on your network, how can you recognize what doesn't belong? In this talk, we'll examine network visibility from both perspectives, highlighting how attackers and defenders approach the same unfamiliar environment with very different objectives. We'll cover practical techniques for building and maintaining meaningful baselines by correlating what you already have: DHCP and DNS logs, network telemetry from Zeek and Suricata, as well as active discovery with Nmap, and existing vulnerability scan data, stitched together in a Jupyter notebook so the gaps between sources become visible. Those gaps are where both your blind spots and your findings live. Every technique here works for teams with limited budgets and no formal asset management platform. Attendees will learn to turn the 'living off the land' approach attackers use daily into a defensive one: continuously discovering assets, identifying changes, enriching detection engineering, and building the context that separates normal operations from malicious behavior. All code and slides will be published on GitHub, so you can run the same workflow against your own environment. Whether you're defending a small business or a large enterprise, you'll leave with strategies for answering one of the most important questions in security: who understands your network better, you or your adversary?

presenters.name: Lennart Koopman ⓘ
presenters.bio: Lennart is the founder of Nzyme, an open source WiFi and Ethernet intrusion detection system (IDS). He previously created the Graylog open source project. A software developer by trade and an active member of the cybersecurity community, Lennart was born and raised in Germany and now lives in Texas.

presenters.name: Matt Gracie ⓘ
presenters.bio: Matthew Gracie is a defensive security specialist with fifteen years of Blue Team experience in higher education, manufacturing, financial services, and healthcare. He is currently a Senior Engineer at Security Onion Solutions, as well as an adjunct professor of Cybersecurity in the graduate school at Canisius University. Matt is also the lead organizer of Infosec 716, a monthly meetup for security enthusiasts in Western New York, and the BSides Buffalo technology conference. He enjoys microcontrollers, mountain bikes, open source security tools, and college hockey, and can be found on Bluesky as @InfosecGoon.

schedule.description: Nzyme is a free and open platform for detecting physical, close-proximity attempts to compromise your network infrastructure. In this talk we will explore the Nzyme platform, how it leverages Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and Ethernet traffic to detect these events, and how its findings can be tied into Security Onion to alert on threats like rogue access points or hidden Bluetooth trackers as soon as they appear.

presenters.name: Josh Brower ⓘ
presenters.bio: Josh Brower has been crashing computers since his teens, and now feels fortunate to be doing it professionally. He has spent most of his career focusing on InfoSec, particularly network and endpoint detection. As a Principal Engineer at Security Onion Solutions, he works on the platform's continual development.

schedule.topic: Sigma Correlations: Everything, Everywhere, All Within 5 Minutes ⓘ
schedule.description: A single failed logon is noise. Twenty failed logons against twenty accounts from one source, followed by one success, needs to be escalated. Standard Sigma rules can only see the first. The new Correlation rules change that: count, threshold, and sequence across multiple events. In this session we will walk through each correlation type and build real detections with them drawing on network, host, authentication, and application logs.

presenters.name: Bryant Treacle ⓘ
presenters.bio: Bryant Treacle has over 25 years of experience in cybersecurity and IT networking across both Department of Defense and commercial environments. He currently serves as a Senior Engineer and Training Manager at Security Onion Solutions LLC, where he focuses on detection engineering, network security monitoring, and endpoint visibility. His work focuses on building practical, real-world detection capabilities for SOC analysts, with an emphasis on enterprise and ICS/OT environments.

schedule.topic: Defending OT/ICS Environments with Security Onion ⓘ
schedule.description: Grounding in the real-world 2021 Oldsmar water treatment attack, where an intruder remotely attempted to spike sodium hydroxide to dangerous levels, this talk breaks down the Modbus/TCP protocol in accessible terms (no prior expertise needed) and walks attendees through a practical defense strategy: gaining network visibility, baselining normal industrial activity, and implementing Suricata rules to detect rogue devices, deviations, and targeted attacks. The session briefly covers adding custom Zeek scripts built to close a gap in native Zeek Modbus parsing and wraps with a live demo.

presenters.name: Doug Burks ⓘ
presenters.bio: Doug Burks started Security Onion in 2008 to provide a comprehensive platform to help folks peel back the layers of their enterprise and make their adversaries cry. Today, Security Onion has over 2,500,000 downloads and is being used by organizations around the world for threat hunting, enterprise security monitoring, and log management. In 2014, Doug started Security Onion Solutions LLC to help those organizations by providing training, professional services, and hardware appliances. Doug is a CEO, public speaker, teacher, former president of the Greater Augusta ISSA, and co-founder of BSides Augusta, but what he really likes the most is catching bad guys.
